oewn-08273889-n.learner: An organized group that tries to gain political power.
examples: She voted for the party that promised to build more schools.

oewn-10422569-n.learner: A person who is involved in a legal case.
examples: Both parties in the lawsuit were asked to appear before the judge.

oewn-02641270-v.learner: To have something as a result that follows logically from it.
examples: Missing the last bus means walking home.

oewn-02748357-v.learner: To be important to a certain degree.
examples: Your letter meant a great deal to me.

oewn-00710669-v.learner: To set someone or something apart for a certain purpose, or to name it for that purpose.
examples: This room was meant for guests, not for storing boxes.

oewn-00732037-v.learner: To have a particular person or thing in mind as the one you are talking about.
examples: When I said someone had been late, I meant you.

oewn-00804608-v.learner: To let something be present, or let an activity go on, without opposing it or forbidding it.
examples: The café allows dogs inside.

oewn-02727313-v.learner: To make something possible or give a chance for it, or to let something be reached or stay.
examples: The plan allows time for questions at the end.
The facts allow only one explanation.
The nurse allowed each child two sweets.

oewn-00726112-v.learner: To give or set aside a supply of something for a particular person or purpose.
examples: The council allowed a large sum for repairing the roads.

oewn-02324649-v.learner: To take an amount off a price, or to give an amount in exchange for something.
examples: The shop allowed us fifty pounds for our old cooker.

oewn-02428446-v.learner: In baseball, to let the other team score.
examples: The pitcher allowed three runs in the first inning.

oewn-05811387-n.learner: A rough calculation of how much there is of something, how great it is, or what it is worth.
examples: Can you give me an idea of how much the repairs will cost?

oewn-07042734-n.learner: In music, the tune that a piece is built on.
examples: The violins bring back the opening idea near the end of the piece.

oewn-06643134-n.learner: A polite way of saying you hope someone is well and happy, usually used in the plural.
examples: Please give your mother my best wishes.

oewn-14031827-n.learner: The way something, such as a machine or a substance, acts or reacts in certain conditions.

oewn-04855493-n.learner: Hope as one of the three virtues named in Christian teaching.

oewn-02736688-v.learner: To have certain words written on it, or to have a certain form.

oewn-00626148-v.learner: To understand something in a certain way, or to give a certain meaning or impression.
examples: She read the letter as a polite refusal.

oewn-00595247-v.learner: To be able to make sense of a language.

oewn-00601387-v.learner: To be a student of a particular subject.

oewn-00924838-v.learner: Of a gauge or measuring tool, to show a certain amount or number.

oewn-00621911-v.learner: To hear someone and understand them.

oewn-00002669-r.learner: Only a very short time before.
